messages:
michael: Heads-up — I'm running an experiment for SLO-driven token caps per route/tier to hit 95th latency targets. Made a prototype scheduler that lowers token budgets when p95 creeps over target. Initial rollout caused regressions on long-context KV-heavy flows so I want feedback.
elaine: can you paste the config + a short profiler snapshot? which routes showed regressions?
samir: saw this yesterday — the int8 kernel path changes the dispatch pattern. For sequences >1024 we get extra KV lookups + kernel stalls. Might be that smaller token caps force more small batches and lose kernel sweet spot.
michael: profiler snippet from yesterday's failing run:
```
route: /chat/assistant (prod)
avg batch size: 5 -> 3 after cap applied
profile: formation 6.2ms, kv_lookup 18.7ms, kernel_dispatch 4.1ms
total p95: 240ms (SLO 200ms)
```
ana: ouch. so reducing token cap reduced batching efficiency and increased kv_lookup dominance. do we have per-route seq-length histograms?
michael: yes — /chat/assistant median seq_out 40, 95th seq_out 680, kv-hit rate ~0.78 for 95th. token cap was 64 then reduced to 32 for tier=free.
jonathan: quick thought — token cap should consider tail sequence length distribution + kv hit probability. If 95th seq_out > cap then we'll split the tail and pay more KV overhead. Suggest a dynamic cap: compute expected p95 from current cap, adjust to meet SLO with a safety margin.
elaine: what about queue policy? we used age_based_prefer_short earlier. That helped latency for short requests but may interleave badly with long KV flows. Maybe per-route policy toggle.
michael: current rollout config (simplified):
```json
{
  "scheduler": "slo_token_cap",
  "routes": {
    "/chat/assistant": {"tier":"prod","base_cap":64,"min":16,"max":256,"queue_policy":"age_based_prefer_short"},
    "/chat/private": {"tier":"enterprise","base_cap":128,"min":64,"max":512,"queue_policy":"fifo"}
  }
}
```
samir: propose adding kernel-awareness: if kernel selection metric shows dispatch to int8 path yields +X ms for batches <B, then enforce min_batch_size or prefer batching until B reached for that kernel.
nana: agree. Also KV cache behavior note — when we split sequences across microbatches, KV fetches duplicate some work because prefix caching isn't reused across microbatch boundaries when cache window isn't shared. We should prefer contiguous token budgets for long tails to maximize KV reuse.
jonathan: rough pseudo for cap adjuster:
```py
for route in routes:
  p95_now = rolling_p95(route, 30m)
  target = slo_p95(route)
  factor = target / max(p95_now, 1)
  new_cap = clamp(round(base_cap * factor), min_cap, max_cap)
  # floor to kernel-friendly boundaries (e.g., multiples of 8)
  new_cap = round_to_boundary(new_cap, 8)
```
elaine: love the kernel-friendly rounding. Also add a cooldown window (5-10m) to avoid oscillation.
michael: results from a local canary with kernel-aware rule + per-route queue policy: /chat/assistant p95 dropped to 195ms, avg cost +3% but SLO met. We still see a small regression for enterprise long batch (private route) when setting fifo -> investig.
deploy-bot: scheduled rollout: slo_token_cap v0.3 -> canary (10%) at 2026-02-18T14:32Z
jonathan: next steps: (1) add kernel latency table to scheduler and floor caps to avoid tiny batches, (2) add per-route queue policy override, (3) add telemetry for microbatch KV reuse rate. Assign: samir(1), elaine(2), ana(3). I'll follow up with a short PR template for the config changes. :thumbsup:
michael: thanks — will track in the perf board and add the canary results. If anyone has more microbench numbers for int8 dispatch vs fp16 at different batch sizes pls drop them here.
